text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan criticizes the military, causing tension ahead of next week's regular monthly meeting of the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK).

- Ministry of education announces that compulsory education will be raised to eight years in 1997. The plan for uninterrupted education for eight years, recommended by the MGK, was slammed by Islamists because it would effectively shut down the middle section of religious schools that currently take pupils at 11.
- Turkish chief of staff Ismail Hakki Karadayi said the MGK was a body created by the constitution and that all its decisions would be implemented.
- Karadayi calls for friendlier relations with Greece.
- The Islamist-led coalition has begun working on a new electoral system. The move caused speculation that the government was preparing for early elections.
- Premier Erbakan says that no one will be able set conditions for Turkey's accession to the European Union.
- Industrial production of Turkey went up by 7.7 in 1996.
- Students in religous high-schools and their parents are worried by the ambiguity surrounding the future of their schools if the eight-year uninterrupted education plan is implemented.
